overview: This single-page Department of State list of papers inventories three records filed under “Iron Mines—Japan.” The entries concern an undisclosed Japanese high-speed ore-smelting invention, Justice Department material on Japan’s iron and steel industry, and a despatch from Kuibyshev enclosing a translation of a Soviet article on Japanese ferrous metallurgy under wartime conditions; the first two entries also direct researchers to related decimal-file references.

subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Iron Mines—Japan
subfiles.about: An archival contents sheet lists three papers relating to Japanese iron mining, smelting, and wartime ferrous metallurgy.
subfiles.summary: The first entry records a Military Attaché report dated December 14, 1935, on a high-speed ore-smelting process reportedly invented by an unnamed Japanese person, whose technical details had not been made public, and refers the reader to 894.20 M.I.D. Reports/42. The second lists a November 18 Justice Department transmission enclosing memoranda on Japan’s iron and steel industry and notes file 894.24. The third lists despatch no. 270, dated March 18, from Kuibyshev in the Soviet Union, associated with Dooman, enclosing translations of a Soviet writer’s article titled “Ferrous Metallurgy in Japan Under War Conditions.”

interest: The sheet is useful as a compact map of U.S. government intelligence and interdepartmental interest in Japan’s iron and steel capacity. It links military reporting, Justice Department memoranda, and Soviet wartime analysis, revealing how technological innovation and industrial preparedness were tracked across otherwise separate parts of the State Department decimal files. Its cross-references may also help historians locate related material filed outside the iron-mines subject folder.
